content: === Introduction ===
The following outline is provided as an overview of and topical guide to cryptography:

Cryptography (or cryptology) – practice and study of hiding information. Modern cryptography intersects the disciplines of mathematics, computer science, and engineering. Applications of cryptography include ATM cards, computer passwords, and electronic commerce.

=== Organizations and selection projects ===

<info> Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) Publication Program – run by NIST to produce standards in many areas to guide operations of the US Federal government; many FIPS publications are ongoing and related to cryptography
<info> American National Standards Institute (ANSI) – standardization process that produces many standards in many areas; some are cryptography related, ongoing)
<info> International Organization for Standardization (ISO) – standardization process produces many standards in many areas; some are cryptography related, ongoing
<info> Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) – standardization process produces many standards in many areas; some are cryptography related, ongoing
<info> Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) – standardization process that produces many standards called RFCs) in many areas; some are cryptography related, ongoing)
<info> National Security Agency (NSA) – internal evaluation/selections, charged with assisting NIST in its cryptographic responsibilities
<info> Government Communications Headquarters (GCHQ) – internal evaluation/selections, a division is charged with developing and recommending cryptographic standards for the UK government
<info> Defence Signals Directorate (DSD) – Australian SIGINT agency, part of ECHELON
<info> Communications Security Establishment (CSE) – Canadian intelligence agency
<info> Data Encryption Standard (DES) – NBS selection process, ended 1976
<info> RIPE – division of the RACE project sponsored by the European Union, ended mid-1980s
<info> Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) – a "break-off" competition sponsored by NIST, ended in 2001
<info> NESSIE Project – an evaluation/selection program sponsored by the European Union, ended in 2002
<info> eSTREAM– program funded by ECRYPT; motivated by the failure of all of the stream ciphers submitted to NESSIE, ended in 2008
<info> CRYPTREC – evaluation/recommendation program sponsored by the Japanese government; draft recommendations published 2003
<info> CrypTool – an e-learning freeware programme in English and German— exhaustive educational tool about cryptography and cryptanalysis
